sections.title: Going somewhere regularly
sections.content: jár ("to go regularly, to attend") is a new regular verb, used together with a destination case to say where someone goes on an ongoing basis — to school, to university, to a class. It's different from megy ("to go"), which is about one trip, not a habit.

items.english: My younger sister still attends school.

sections.content: jár takes -ba/-be or -ra/-re, not -ban/-ben, even though attending feels like just being somewhere — Hungarian treats a habit as repeated trips into or onto a place, so keep the directional case: iskolába jár, egyetemre jár.
